Spanish micro-learning · 01
High intermediate
Expressing unexpected closeness

Hace pocos días que te conozco y parece como si hiciera muchos años.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
I’ve only known you for a few days, but it feels as though it had been many years.
◆ Power chunk
parece como si + imperfect subjunctive
◇ Grammar insight
«Como si» introduces an unreal comparison. Spanish steps away from reality with the imperfect subjunctive: «hiciera».
↗ Native upgrade
Parece que nos conociéramos de toda la vida.
It feels as if we had known each other forever.
× Common mistake
como si hace muchos años
como si hiciera muchos años
◌ Pronunciation
Link «días_que» smoothly. Avoid inserting a full pause between the two words.
◎ Cultural feel
This sounds warm and emotionally direct. It fits a sincere, intimate conversation better than casual small talk.
✦ Memory hook
«Como si» opens an imaginary world. Once the comparison leaves reality, the verb enters the subjunctive.

Spanish micro-learning · 02
High intermediate
Giving constructive feedback

Lo que propones tiene sentido, pero quizá habría que darle una vuelta más antes de tomar una decisión.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
What you’re proposing makes sense, but perhaps we should think it through a little more before making a decision.
◆ Power chunk
darle una vuelta a algo
◇ Grammar insight
«Habría que + infinitivo» gives an impersonal recommendation. It sounds collaborative and softer than «tenemos que».
↗ Native upgrade
La idea va bien encaminada, pero todavía le falta un poco de desarrollo.
The idea is heading in the right direction, but it still needs a little more development.
× Common mistake
pensar más sobre ello
darle una vuelta más
◌ Pronunciation
Link «vuelta_más» smoothly so the phrase feels continuous rather than word-by-word.
◎ Cultural feel
This phrasing works well professionally because it questions the idea without directly criticizing the person.
✦ Memory hook
Imagine physically turning an idea around in your hands. «Darle una vuelta» means examining it from another angle.

Spanish micro-learning · 03
High intermediate
Changing your mind

Cuanto más lo pienso, más claro tengo que deberíamos esperar.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
The more I think about it, the clearer it becomes to me that we should wait.
◆ Power chunk
Cuanto más..., más...
◇ Grammar insight
This paired structure shows two things increasing together. The first clause creates the condition; the second gives the result.
↗ Native upgrade
Después de pensarlo bien, creo que lo más sensato sería esperar.
After thinking it through, I think the most sensible thing would be to wait.
× Common mistake
Mientras más lo pienso...
Cuanto más lo pienso...
◌ Pronunciation
Keep «más_lo» connected. Avoid a heavy pause after «más» in the first half.
◎ Cultural feel
In Spain, «cuanto más» is the safest polished form. «Mientras más» is common in many parts of Latin America.
✦ Memory hook
Picture two rising lines: more thought leads to more certainty.

Spanish micro-learning · 04
High intermediate
Interrupting politely

Perdona que te interrumpa, pero hay un detalle importante que deberíamos tener en cuenta.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
Sorry to interrupt you, but there is an important detail that we should take into account.
◆ Power chunk
Perdona que + subjunctive
◇ Grammar insight
After «perdona que», Spanish normally uses the subjunctive because the speaker is reacting to an action they are performing.
↗ Native upgrade
No quiero cortarte, pero creo que conviene aclarar una cosa antes de seguir.
I don’t want to cut you off, but I think we should clarify one thing before continuing.
× Common mistake
Perdona que te interrumpo
Perdona que te interrumpa
◌ Pronunciation
The stress falls on «rrump» in «interrumpa». Keep the double r strong but brief.
◎ Cultural feel
This is direct enough to enter the conversation but respectful enough for meetings, family discussions, and formal settings.
✦ Memory hook
The apology opens a small door; the subjunctive lets the interruption pass through politely.

Spanish micro-learning · 05

Giving thoughtful advice

Si estuviera en tu lugar, empezaría por la opción más sencilla.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
If I were in your position, I would start with the simplest option.
◆ Power chunk
Si estuviera..., empezaría...
◇ Grammar insight
Use imperfect subjunctive in the hypothetical «si» clause and conditional in the result.
↗ Native upgrade
Yo, en tu situación, iría paso a paso y evitaría complicarlo desde el principio.
In your situation, I would go step by step and avoid making it complicated from the start.
× Common mistake
Si estaría en tu lugar
Si estuviera en tu lugar
◌ Pronunciation
Let «estuviera_en» flow together. The adjacent vowels should not become two heavy syllables.
◎ Cultural feel
Framing advice as a personal hypothetical makes it sound supportive rather than commanding.
✦ Memory hook
The imaginary situation lives in the subjunctive; the imagined action lives in the conditional.

Spanish micro-learning · 06
High intermediate
Expressing relief

Menos mal que me avisaste; si no, habría llegado al lugar equivocado.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
Good thing you told me; otherwise, I would have arrived at the wrong place.
◆ Power chunk
Menos mal que...
◇ Grammar insight
«Habría llegado» is conditional perfect. It describes an unreal past result that did not happen.
↗ Native upgrade
Por suerte me lo dijiste a tiempo; de lo contrario, habría sido un desastre.
Luckily, you told me in time; otherwise, it would have been a disaster.
× Common mistake
Menos malo que...
Menos mal que...
◌ Pronunciation
Say «menos_mal» as one rhythmic unit. The expression is usually delivered quickly and with feeling.
◎ Cultural feel
«Menos mal» is extremely common in everyday Spanish and often carries more feeling than a literal «fortunately».
✦ Memory hook
Something bad almost happened, but there was ‘less bad’: «menos mal».

Spanish micro-learning · 07
High intermediate
De-escalating a disagreement

No quiero que esto se convierta en una discusión; prefiero que intentemos entendernos.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
I don’t want this to turn into an argument; I’d rather we try to understand each other.
◆ Power chunk
No quiero que..., prefiero que...
◇ Grammar insight
Both wishes involve a different subject, so Spanish uses the subjunctive: «se convierta» and «intentemos».
↗ Native upgrade
No merece la pena discutir por esto; veamos si podemos encontrar un punto medio.
This isn’t worth arguing about; let’s see whether we can find some middle ground.
× Common mistake
prefiero que intentamos
prefiero que intentemos
◌ Pronunciation
Link «que_esto» naturally, and place the strongest stress in «conVIERta».
◎ Cultural feel
This sounds firm but conciliatory. It is useful with a partner, relative, or coworker when tension starts rising.
✦ Memory hook
A preference creates an alternate outcome. That desired, not-yet-real outcome enters the subjunctive.

Spanish micro-learning · 08
High intermediate
Explaining a delayed reply

No es que no quisiera contestarte; es que necesitaba aclarar algunas cosas antes de hacerlo.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
It’s not that I didn’t want to reply to you; I just needed to clear a few things up before doing so.
◆ Power chunk
No es que..., es que...
◇ Grammar insight
«No es que» rejects a possible interpretation and takes the subjunctive «quisiera». «Es que» then introduces the real explanation.
↗ Native upgrade
No te estaba ignorando; simplemente no quería responderte sin tener toda la información.
I wasn’t ignoring you; I simply didn’t want to answer without having all the information.
× Common mistake
No es que no quería contestarte
No es que no quisiera contestarte
◌ Pronunciation
Treat «es_que» as one light rhythmic unit; the word «que» should remain unstressed.
◎ Cultural feel
This protects the relationship while explaining your intention. It sounds less defensive than simply listing excuses.
✦ Memory hook
The first half rejects a false possibility, so it uses subjunctive. The second half gives the real reason.

Spanish micro-learning · 09
High intermediate
Making a careful commitment

Haré todo lo posible por terminarlo hoy, aunque no puedo prometerte que esté listo a tiempo.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
I’ll do everything I can to finish it today, although I can’t promise you that it will be ready on time.
◆ Power chunk
hacer todo lo posible por + infinitive
◇ Grammar insight
«Haré» commits to the effort. After the negated «no puedo prometerte que», the uncertain result takes the subjunctive «esté».
↗ Native upgrade
Voy a intentar sacarlo adelante hoy, pero prefiero no asegurarte algo que quizá no pueda cumplir.
I’m going to try to get it done today, but I’d rather not guarantee something I may not be able to deliver.
× Common mistake
no puedo prometerte que está listo
no puedo prometerte que esté listo
◌ Pronunciation
Connect «todo_lo_posible» and «prometerte_que_esté» so the sentence flows in larger thought groups.
◎ Cultural feel
This is strong professional Spanish: you commit fully to the effort without pretending an uncertain deadline is guaranteed.
✦ Memory hook
The effort is certain, so it stays indicative. The promised result is uncertain, so it moves into the subjunctive.

Spanish micro-learning · 10
High intermediate
Regretting an unreal past

De haber sabido que ibas a venir, habría organizado el día de otra manera.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
Had I known you were coming, I would have organized the day differently.
◆ Power chunk
De haber sabido..., habría...
◇ Grammar insight
«De + perfect infinitive» is a concise alternative to «si hubiera sabido». The unreal result uses the conditional perfect «habría organizado».
↗ Native upgrade
Si me lo hubieras dicho antes, habría reservado más tiempo para estar contigo.
Had you told me earlier, I would have set aside more time to be with you.
× Common mistake
Si habría sabido...
Si hubiera sabido... / De haber sabido...
◌ Pronunciation
Let «haber_sabido» and «habría_organizado» flow across the adjacent vowels instead of separating every word.
◎ Cultural feel
«De haber sabido» sounds polished and compact. It appears often in careful conversation, interviews, and written Spanish.
✦ Memory hook
«De haber» compresses the unreal past condition; «habría» delivers the consequence that never happened.

Spanish micro-learning · 11
High intermediate
Negotiating a compromise

Podríamos dejarlo así por ahora, siempre que revisemos los detalles más adelante.

Native neural Spanish audio
Default: 0.85×One recording · one player
Natural English
We could leave it like this for now, provided that we review the details later.
◆ Power chunk
siempre que + subjunctive
◇ Grammar insight
The conditional «podríamos» softens the proposal. «Siempre que» introduces a required condition and takes the subjunctive «revisemos».
↗ Native upgrade
Me parece un buen punto de partida, con la condición de que volvamos a revisarlo la semana que viene.
It seems like a good starting point to me, on the condition that we review it again next week.
× Common mistake
siempre que revisamos los detalles
siempre que revisemos los detalles
◌ Pronunciation
Link «siempre_que» and «detalles_más» so the condition sounds like one complete unit.
◎ Cultural feel
This language is collaborative rather than all-or-nothing. It is ideal for negotiation, planning, and resolving minor disagreements.
✦ Memory hook
The agreement opens only if the condition unlocks it. That pending condition takes the subjunctive.
